raw.body:
**Update: we've now captured the loop state in the act — this is no longer a hypothesis.**

We wrapped `Node.prototype.insertBefore` via `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` with a guard that dumps state and throws after 200,000 calls (a normal load of this page performs ~50). On the 2nd reload during an affected window, the guard tripped **inside `$RV`**:

```
stack: at Node.insertBefore (<anonymous>:19:19)
       at $RV (https://<page-url>:1:69928)

parent (f):  DIV#S:10  hidden=true      ← insertion parent is the *hidden segment container itself*
ref (c):     <!--/$--> comment, parentNode === DIV#S:10, f.contains(ref) === true
moved nodes: DIV#top, DIV#description-tab, DIV#review-tab, DIV#recommendation-tab, NAV, … (cycling)
sameContainerCycle: true                 ← node.parentNode === f && ref.parentNode === f
parent childCount: 22, first children: <!--&--> <!--&--> <!--&--> <!--$--> <!--$~-->
```

So the degenerate case is: for one pair, the insertion parent `f` **is the segment container `e` itself** (which `$RV` has just detached via `e.parentNode.removeChild(e)`), and the reference node `c` found by the marker walk is a `/$` comment **inside `e`**. `for(;e.firstChild;)f.insertBefore(e.firstChild,c)` then rotates `e`'s own child list forever — the same elements cycle indefinitely. Each call also queues MutationObserver records for observers on the page, explaining the unbounded multi-GB memory growth.

Structural context: the page has **nested Suspense boundaries** — in captured responses, `<template id="B:10">` (inner boundary placeholder) ships *inside* `<div hidden id="S:13">` (an outer boundary's content segment). The reveal appears to be order-sensitive when both pairs land in the same `$RB` batch: processing a pair while its placeholder still lives inside another (hidden / just-detached) segment produces the `f === e` / `c ∈ e` state above.

Two additional data points:

- Replaying a fully-loaded, well-formed snapshot of the same document as a single non-streamed response (which forces maximum batching — all 15 `$RC` calls in one tick) does **not** reproduce. The pathological state only arises with real streaming timing, matching the intermittency (0%–90% repro rate across hours on the same build, tracking server latency).
- Defensive fix suggestion: in `$RV`, validate the insertion position before the move loop (e.g. `if (e === f || e.contains(c))` → mark the boundary client-rendered instead), or bound the loop — so a raced marker state degrades to a broken boundary instead of hanging the page at 100% CPU.

Happy to share the guard probe script and full dump, or run instrumented builds.
